newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - Nov 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - Nov 7.

text.p: These are significant items in the Ivorian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these items and does not vouch for their accuracy. FRATERNITE MATIN - Prime Minister Daniel Kablan Duncan says Ivory Coast's economy is growing, with Gross Domestic Product on course for at least 10 percent in 1996; 10 percent more jobs created in manufacturing industry. - Air Afrique employees stage sit-in to protest against plan by the multi-national carrier's outgoing French head Yves Roland-Billecart to sell two Airbus 300 B4s to Iran; say new management, which could be selected at a meeting in Abidjan of member countries' heads of state on November 11, should make such decisions. Flights largely unaffected apart from long delay on a Dakar-Abidjan flight LA VOIE - Prime Minister Duncan refuses to admit the extent of poverty in Ivory Coast, says the opposition Ivorian Popular Front daily, quoting report from National Statistics Institute putting the level at 70 percent. Duncan told a Wednesday news conference that the level was 30 percent at the most. - Head of French employers' association delegation tells Ivory Coast that they want no special treatment because of privileged links between France and its former colony; treat us like the Japonese, the Germans and the Italians, Michel Roussin tells Franco-Ivorian business seminar LE JOUR - Prime Minister Duncan says Ivory Coast expects to pay off its internal debt -- 113 billion CFA francs -- by the end of 1996 - Expo-CI 96 trade fair opens today
